sentiment.rationale: The document shows a genuine operational inflection: NII guidance was meaningfully raised from a prior expectation of a $100-200 million decline to an actual $100 million increase, and management explicitly guided that Q2 2024 will be the NII trough with growth in the back half of the year. This is a clear forward guidance raise on a core metric, not just a backward-looking beat. The score is tempered by the FDIC special assessment (a one-time item) and cautious language on commercial real estate credit, but the organic NII trajectory and confident expense management represent real momentum.

summary.revenue: $25.8 billion, down 2% year-over-year ($440 million decrease), including higher investment banking and asset management fees and lower net interest income.
summary.eps: Reported diluted EPS of $0.76; adjusted diluted EPS (excluding FDIC special assessment) of $0.83.
summary.guidance: NII expected to approach $14 billion on an FTE basis in Q2 2024, which is expected to be the low point, with growth in the back half of 2024. Expense expected to trend down through the year. Low single-digit loan growth and moderate deposit growth assumed.
summary.margin: Net interest yield (FTE) of 1.99%, down 21 bps year-over-year, up 2 bps from Q4 2023. Adjusted efficiency ratio of 64% (excluding FDIC assessment).
key_risks: Higher deposit costs continue to pressure NII, partially offset by higher asset yields.
Net charge-offs increased to $1.5 billion, driven by credit card seasoning and commercial real estate office exposures.
Commercial real estate office portfolio: $72 billion exposure, with ~12% NPL ratio and $0.3 billion in Q1 2024 charge-offs.
Uncertainty around Basel III endgame capital rules and their finalization.
Potential for higher-for-longer interest rates to impact deposit mix shift and loan demand.
key_opportunities: Investment banking fees grew 35% year-over-year to $1.6 billion, with market share improvement of 115 bps.
Record revenue in Global Wealth & Investment Management ($5.6 billion, up 5% YoY) with record client balances of nearly $4 trillion.
Sales and trading revenue (ex-DVA) of $5.2 billion, the best first quarter in over a decade.
Continued organic growth: 245,000 net new consumer checking accounts (21st consecutive quarter of growth), 7,300 net new wealth relationships.
Digital engagement driving cost savings: 3.4 billion digital logins, 50% of sales through digital channels, Zelle transactions surpassing checks plus cash withdrawals.
Strong capital position: CET1 ratio of 11.8%, $31 billion above regulatory minimum, allowing for continued shareholder returns ($4.4 billion returned in Q1).
